Akron · Kent · Canton

Akron 45

Downtown, Highland Square, North Hill & Firestone Park

  1. Must see · Burgers, Drive-ins & Diners · Akron

    Swensons Drive-In (original, Wallhaven)

    Pop Swenson started selling burgers from his station wagon at Buchtel High in 1933 and opened this South Hawkins drive-in in 1934; it's still the flagship of Akron's signature burger, the Galley Boy, run to your car by sprinting curb-hops. Signal Akron readers' Best Burger 2025; Beacon Journal readers' bracket winner 2026; Reader's Digest's best burger in Ohio.

    40 S Hawkins Ave, Akron, OH 44313

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Signal Akron, Ohio Magazine, Akron Beacon Journal, Cleveland Jewish News, Akron Life

  2. Must see · Akron

    Stan Hywet Hall & Gardens

    The 65-room Tudor Revival country estate Goodyear co-founder F.A. Seiberling built in 1912–15, with 70 acres of Warren Manning landscapes and an English garden — Akron's grandest house, a National Historic Landmark and the place Alcoholics Anonymous was born (Henrietta Seiberling introduced Bill W. to Dr. Bob in the Gate Lodge, 1935).

    Look for ARCH

    714 N Portage Path, Akron, OH 44303

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Historical Marker Database, Ohio & Erie Canalway (National Heritage Area), Akron Life

  3. Must see · Akron

    Akron Civic Theatre

    John Eberson's 1929 Loew's atmospheric movie palace — a Moorish courtyard under a domed ceiling of twinkling stars and drifting clouds — restored and still Akron's main stage for touring shows and concerts.

    Look for ARCH

    182 S Main St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Heritage Ohio, NATIONAL PARK SVC, Cinema Treasures, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Akron

    Dr. Bob's Home (birthplace of Alcoholics Anonymous)

    The 1914 house where Dr. Bob Smith and Bill Wilson worked out AA's principles and recruited its first members in 1935 — a National Historic Landmark (2012) kept as a museum and a pilgrimage site for the millions in 12-step recovery.

    Look for ARCH

    855 Ardmore Ave, Akron, OH 44302

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NATIONAL PARK SVC, Akron/Summit CVB, Akron Life

  5. Must see · Akron

    Sojourner Truth Legacy Plaza

    Where Sojourner Truth gave her 'Ain't I a Woman?' speech at the 1851 Ohio Women's Rights Convention (Old Stone Church site). A plaza and statue were dedicated on the speech's anniversary, May 29, 2024, beside the 1981 Ohio Historical Marker. Free.

    Look for ARCH

    37 N High St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by ATLAS OBSCURA, REMARKABLEOHIO, Associated Press, WKYC Channel 3

  6. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Akron

    Luigi's Restaurant

    Downtown Akron's Italian landmark since 1949 (Ciriello family), its brick entry papered with signed celebrity photos and a line out the door late at night. Signal Akron readers' Best Pizza 2025; No. 1 pizza and No. 1 Italian in Akron Life's 2026 330 Flavor Awards.

    105 N Main St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Signal Akron, Akron Life, Scene (Northeast Ohio alt-weekly), Ohio Magazine

  7. Must see · Akron

    Akron Art Museum

    Akron's art museum: the 1899 Renaissance Revival former post office joined to Coop Himmelb(l)au's 2007 'Roof Cloud' steel-and-glass Knight Building — modern and contemporary American art, free admission.

    Look for MUS

    1 S High St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Encyclopedia of Cleveland History (CWRU), Dezeen

  8. Must see · Akron

    Derby Downs (All-American Soap Box Derby)

    The WPA-built 1936 hill track in southeast Akron where kids in gravity-powered cars have raced the All-American Soap Box Derby world championship every July since 1946.

    Look for ICON

    789 Derby Downs, Akron, OH 44306

    Recommended by Akron/Summit CVB, Spectrum News 1 Ohio, OFFICIAL SITE

  9. Must see · American & New American · Akron

    Diamond Grille

    Akron's frozen-in-time 1935 steakhouse — neon sign, phone booth, Sputnik chandeliers — and the haunt of tour pros like Tiger Woods during Firestone weeks. No. 1 Best Restaurant in the 330 (with sister Kingfish), Akron Life 330 Flavor Awards 2026.

    77 W Market St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Akron Life, Ohio Magazine, Akron Beacon Journal

  10. Must see · Akron

    Akron Zoo

    Compact, well-loved accredited zoo on Perkins Park in west Akron — Komodo dragons, snow leopards, Grizzly Ridge and the Journey to Madagascar building.

    Look for FAM

    500 Edgewood Ave, Akron, OH 44307

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Akron Life

  11. Must see · Frozen Custard, Ice Cream & Sweets · Akron

    Strickland's Frozen Custard (original, Triplett Blvd)

    Bill and Florence Strickland opened this walk-up stand in 1936 on the same spot it still occupies; Bill, an Akron Pure Milk man, built his own batch freezer to keep air out of the custard. A spring-to-fall Akron ritual and a WKYC top-15 Northeast Ohio ice cream pick.

    1809 Triplett Blvd, Akron, OH 44306

    Recommended by Wikipedia, WKYC Channel 3

  12. Must see · Nepali, Bhutanese & South Asian · Akron

    Saffron Patch

    Family-owned North Indian kitchen in the Merriman Valley since 1997. Signal Akron readers' Best Ethnic/International Food in both 2025 and 2026, and a 330 Flavor Awards Best Indian winner; Akron Life features it in its Merriman Valley guide.

    1238 Weathervane Ln, Akron, OH 44313

    Recommended by Signal Akron, Signal Akron, Akron Life

  13. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Akron

    DeCheco's Pizzeria

    Family-run Firestone Park pizzeria since 1993. Won the Akron Beacon Journal's 2025 best-pizza-in-Akron reader bracket (nearly 4,000 votes) and Signal Akron's 2026 Best Pizza after two years as runner-up. Second shop at 1581 Canton Rd, Ellet.

    2075 S Main St, Akron, OH 44301

    Recommended by Signal Akron, Akron Beacon Journal, Akron Beacon Journal

  14. Worth the detour · Akron

    Cascade Locks Park & Mustill Store

    The staircase of seven Ohio & Erie Canal locks that lifted boats 70 ft to the Akron Summit, the canal's highest point; the restored c.1847 Mustill Store at Lock 15 is now a seasonal canal museum on the Towpath Trail.

    Look for ARCH

    Cascade Locks Park, N Howard St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Akron/Summit CVB, Historical Marker Database, Akron Life

  15. Worth the detour · Akron

    Glendale Steps

    242 hand-dressed sandstone steps the WPA laid in 1936–37 up a 200-ft slope — Gertrude Seiberling's idea, designed by Warren Manning — a Depression-era monument in a city the rubber layoffs hit hard.

    Look for ODD

    Glendale Ave & S Walnut St, Akron, OH 44302

    Recommended by ATLAS OBSCURA, REMARKABLEOHIO, Signal Akron, The Living New Deal

  16. Worth the detour · Akron

    Summit Lake Nature Center & Summit Lake Trail

    Summit Metro Parks' urban nature center on Summit Lake — the Ohio & Erie Canal's high point — born of the Knight/Kresge-backed Reimagining the Civic Commons program, with the 2.75-mile Summit Lake Trail looping the lake onto the Towpath. Free.

    Look for PARK

    411 Ira Ave, Akron, OH 44301

    Recommended by SUMMIT METRO PARKS, Spectrum News 1 Ohio, Landscape Architecture Magazine, Signal Akron

  17. Worth the detour · Akron

    Goodyear Airdock

    The 1929 airship hangar beside Akron Fulton airport — at completion the largest building in the world without interior supports, big enough to make its own indoor weather; it built the Navy's Akron and Macon. Seen from outside (private).

    Look for ODD

    1210 Massillon Rd, Akron, OH 44306

    Recommended by Wikipedia, ATLAS OBSCURA, Docomomo US

  18. Worth the detour · Akron

    Perkins Stone Mansion & John Brown House

    Summit County Historical Society's two houses on Akron's west side: Col. Simon Perkins's 1837 Greek Revival stone mansion, and across the road the c.1830 house abolitionist John Brown rented from Perkins in 1844–54 while they ran a sheep and wool partnership.

    Look for ARCH

    550 Copley Rd, Akron, OH 44320

    Recommended by Wikipedia, OFFICIAL SITE, Akron/Summit CVB

  19. Worth the detour · Akron

    7 17 Credit Union Park (Akron RubberDucks)

    Downtown's 1997 HOK-designed ballpark (Canal Park until 2025), home of the Double-A Akron RubberDucks (Guardians affiliate), with the Ohio & Erie Canal running behind the left-field wall.

    Look for ENT

    300 S Main St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Stadium Journey, The Ballpark Guide

  20. Worth the detour · Akron

    Quaker Square

    Ferdinand Schumacher's oat mills became Quaker Oats; its 36 120-ft concrete grain silos (1932) were later turned into a hotel with perfectly round rooms — now University of Akron dorms, with the complex slated for a hotel revival.

    Look for ODD

    135 S Broadway St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Signal Akron, Spectrum News 1 Ohio

  21. Worth the detour · Akron

    Glendale Cemetery & Civil War Memorial Chapel

    Akron's 1839 rural garden cemetery (88 acres, National Register) — rubber barons and founders in a wooded ravine, and the restored 1876 Gothic Revival chapel the GAR's Buckley Post built for Summit County's Civil War dead.

    Look for ARCH

    150 Glendale Ave, Akron, OH 44302

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NATIONAL PARK SVC, Akron Life

  22. Worth the detour · Akron

    Hower House Museum

    28-room Second Empire Italianate mansion (1871) of 'Father of Akron Industry' John Henry Hower, designed by Akron Plan architect Jacob Snyder; deeded to the University of Akron in 1970 and on the National Register (1973). Open for tours with the Hower family's world-travel collections.

    Look for ARCH

    60 Fir Hill, Akron, OH 44304

    Recommended by OFFICIAL SITE, NATIONAL PARK SVC, Smithsonian Magazine Museum Day venues

  23. Worth the detour · Akron

    Lock 3 Park

    Downtown Akron's civic park on the Ohio & Erie Canal, reopened in November 2024 after a $17.5M rebuild with a performance pavilion, gardens and winter ice-skating ribbon; home of the Akron Children's Museum. Free.

    Look for PARK

    200 S Main St, Akron, OH 44308

    Recommended by Ideastream Public Media (WKSU), Akron Beacon Journal, News 5 Cleveland (WEWS)

  24. Worth the detour · Akron

    E.J. Thomas Performing Arts Hall

    The University of Akron's 2,955-seat hall (1973, opened with a Carlos Chávez world premiere), home of the Akron Symphony and Broadway tours presented with Playhouse Square.

    Look for ENT

    198 Hill St, Akron, OH 44325

    Recommended by Wikipedia, OFFICIAL SITE, Playhouse Square

    Parasson's Italian Restaurant

    The Parasson family's restaurant traces to 1940s downtown Akron and Tonyo's Pizza in Barberton; the Beacon Journal calls a visit 'a trip to the past' and Akron Life readers ranked it No. 2 Italian in the 330 (2026).

    959 E Waterloo Rd, Akron, OH 44306

    Recommended by Akron Beacon Journal, Akron Life, WKYC Channel 3

    1351 East Ave, Akron, OH 44307

  29. Worth the detour · Akron

    Sand Run Metro Park

    995-acre Summit Metro Park opened in 1929 along the Sand Run Parkway ford, with 1930s Civilian Conservation Corps shelters and the Mingo Trail through oak-beech woods into the Seiberling Nature Realm. Free.

    1300 Sand Run Rd (Sand Run Pkwy), Akron, OH 44313

    Kenmore Boulevard Historic District

    Kenmore Blvd (12th–17th St SW; pin at Lay's Guitar Shop, 974 Kenmore Blvd), Akron, OH 44314

  38. Deep cut · Akron

    Firestone Metro Park

    258-acre Summit Metro Parks unit begun with a 1949 gift from Firestone Tire & Rubber: wetlands and marshy meadows along the Tuscarawas River and the old canal-feeder Tuscarawas Race, a sledding hill and 175+ recorded bird species.

    Look for PARK

    2620 Harrington Rd, Akron, OH 44319

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Akron Life, Signal Akron

  39. Deep cut · Akron

    Goodyear Theater

    Goodyear Tire & Rubber's 1920 company hall (1,686-seat auditorium, gym, classrooms) on the old East End campus, reopened in 2016 as a 1,450-seat concert theater anchoring the East End redevelopment. NRHP-listed as Goodyear Hall; covered by Ideastream and Akron Life.

    Look for ENT

    1201 E Market St, Akron, OH 44305

    Recommended by Ideastream Public Media (WKSU), Akron Life, Wikipedia

Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit 26

  1. Must see · Frozen Custard, Ice Cream & Sweets · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Blue Door Cafe & Bakery

    Marine-veteran pastry chef Michael Bruno's 2009 café — No. 6 on Yelp's national Top 100 Brunch Spots (2024, per WKYC) and a Cleveland Magazine, Scene and Akron Life favorite.

    1970 State Rd, Cuyahoga Falls, OH 44223

    Recommended by Akron Life, Scene (Northeast Ohio alt-weekly), WKYC Channel 3, Cleveland Magazine

  2. Must see · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Gorge Metro Park

    Summit Metro Parks' gorge of the Cuyahoga River at the falls the city is named for — the Gorge Trail along sandstone ledges to Mary Campbell Cave ('Old Maid's Kitchen'), where a captive 1759 girl was held, below the High Level Bridge.

    Look for PARK

    1160 Front St, Cuyahoga Falls, OH 44221

    Recommended by SUMMIT METRO PARKS, Akron Life, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Hudson Historic District & Village Green

    A New England village transplanted to the Western Reserve: Greek Revival and Federal houses around the green and James Ellsworth's 1912 clock tower, with Western Reserve Academy ('the Yale of the West') and its 1838 Loomis Observatory a short walk away.

    Look for ARCH

    Main St (OH-91) & Aurora St, Hudson, OH 44236

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Summit County Historical Society, SAH Archipedia

  4. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Russo's

    Chef-owner David Russo's Italian-Cajun roadhouse, opened August 2002 on State Road (a Peninsula address, though the building is in Cuyahoga Falls), with the bar wrapped around the hot line. Russo spent 13 years in Louisiana kitchens under Paul Prudhomme and Emeril Lagasse. Reviewed by Cleveland Magazine ('Down South') and Cleveland Scene ('Russo's on the Rise'), featured by Akron Life, and listed among Akron Life's 2026 330 Flavor Awards results.

    4895 State Rd, Peninsula, OH 44264

    Recommended by Cleveland Magazine, Scene (Northeast Ohio alt-weekly), Akron Life

  5. Must see · American & New American · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Dean Martin's Lanning's

    Bath Township's special-occasion steakhouse over Yellow Creek (opened 1970); bought in 2020, renovated (~$2M) and relaunched as Dean Martin's Lanning's with tuxedoed service and a dress code. Cleveland Magazine: 'a classic Akron restaurant reimagined'; Akron Life feature on the transformation; Wine Spectator Award of Excellence (2022).

    826 N Cleveland-Massillon Rd, Akron, OH 44333

    Recommended by Cleveland Magazine, Akron Life

  6. Worth the detour · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Twins Days Festival (Glen Chamberlin Park)

    Every first full weekend of August since 1976, ~2,000 sets of twins converge on Twinsburg — the world's largest gathering of twins, in the town named for Moses and Aaron Wilcox, the identical twins who bought it in 1819.

    Look for ODD

    Glen Chamberlin Park, 10260 Ravenna Rd, Twinsburg, OH 44087

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Ohio Magazine, Mental Floss, Akron Beacon Journal

  7. Worth the detour · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Deep Lock Quarry Metro Park

    73-acre Summit Metro Park (not an NPS unit) south of Peninsula: Berea-sandstone quarries opened in 1825 for the Ohio & Erie Canal, cast-off millstones from Ferdinand Schumacher's oat mills (later Quaker Oats) and the canal's deepest lock, on the 1.4-mile Quarry Trail. Free.

    Look for PARK

    5779 Riverview Rd, Peninsula, OH 44264

    Recommended by SUMMIT METRO PARKS, NATIONAL PARK SVC, Akron Life, Trek Ohio

  8. Worth the detour · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Tallmadge Circle & First Congregational Church

    A white Federal-style church (1821–25) standing alone inside the town's eight-spoke traffic circle — the Western Reserve's most photographed meetinghouse, which marked its bicentennial in 2025.

    Look for ARCH

    115 Tallmadge Circle, Tallmadge, OH 44278

    Recommended by SAH Archipedia, Ideastream Public Media (WKSU), Summit County Historical Society

  9. Worth the detour · Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson & North Summit

    Liberty Park & Twinsburg Ledges

    Summit Metro Parks' largest natural area (3,000+ acres): the Twinsburg Ledges' conglomerate cliffs and glacial slump blocks, and an accessible nature center with live native animals.

    Look for PARK

    9999 Liberty Rd, Twinsburg, OH 44087

    Recommended by SUMMIT METRO PARKS, Trek Ohio, Twinsburg Bicentennial (city history project)

    Completed in 1836, the arched Kent Dam is the oldest masonry dam in Ohio and the only one tied to a canal lock (the Pennsylvania & Ohio Canal); bypassed in 2004 to free the river, it was kept because Kent loves it — the waterfall centrepiece of a riverside park and the old mill district.

68 sights and 82 places to eat across Akron, the north-Summit towns up toward the Cuyahoga line (Cuyahoga Falls, Stow, Hudson), Kent & Portage County, Barberton and Wadsworth, and Canton, North Canton & Massillon. Each is traceable to the source that named it. The canon is its own: Serbian-style Barberton chicken with hot rice, the Swenson’s Galley Boy, Strickland’s frozen custard, Taggart’s Bittner, Bender’s Tavern and North Hill’s Nepali & Bhutanese kitchens — plus the Pro Football Hall of Fame, Stan Hywet, the McKinley memorial and the May 4 site at Kent State.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The region’s canon is its own: Serbian-immigrant Barberton chicken (lard-fried, with hot rice and vinegar slaw), the Swenson’s Galley Boy and its curb-hops, Strickland’s frozen custard, Canton’s Taggart’s Bittner and Bender’s Tavern, Akron’s old Italian houses, and North Hill’s Nepali & Bhutanese table, sourced to the Akron Beacon Journal, Canton Repository and Signal Akron. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to at least two credible sources (or one institution — James Beard, NPS) — the Akron Beacon Journal, Canton Repository, Record-Courier, Signal Akron, Akron Life, regional magazines and TV, Summit Metro Parks, Atlas Obscura, vetted creators and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
